items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit affirmed summary judgment for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services in a Title VII sex discrimination and retaliation case brought by employee Jack Kahriger. Kahriger claimed he was demoted in retaliation for supporting a colleague's EEO complaint and that similarly situated male managers received more favorable treatment. The court found that Kahriger failed to establish a prima facie case of sex discrimination and that no causal connection existed between his protected activity and his demotion.

items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit affirmed dismissal of a putative class action brought by Julie Thomas against the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission and TransCore LP regarding E-ZPass toll charges. Thomas claimed she was incorrectly charged $950 in penalties despite properly mounting her transponder and brought claims for breach of contract, unjust enrichment, fraud, and consumer protection violations. The court held that Thomas's non-contract claims were barred by Pennsylvania's gist-of-the-action doctrine because they rested on contractual duties.

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain MD Helicopters, LLC (MDHI) Model 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, and 500N helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of mechanical damage to the main transmission drive shaft coupling (coupling). This AD requires a one-time visual inspection of the couplings for cracks of the splines and, depending on the results, replacement of the couplings. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA, the Agency, or we) is announcing the availability of one additional draft chapter of a multichapter draft guidance for industry titled “Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food.” This multichapter draft guidance, when finalized, will explain FDA's current thinking on how to comply with the requirements for hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls under FDA's regulation titled “Current Good Manufacturing Practice, Hazard Analysis, and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food.” The newly available draft chapter is titled “Chapter 12: Control of Chemical Hazards.” This draft guidance is not final nor is it in effect at this time.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY 31 CFR Part 36 [TREAS-DO-2026-0529] RIN 1505-AC96 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Prohibition on Large Institutional Investor Purchases of Single-Family Homes AGENCY: Department of the Treasury. ACTION: Notice of
items.summary: The Department of the Treasury (Treasury) is issuing this proposed rule to carry out the purposes of section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (the Act or the ROAD Act). Section 1001 of the ROAD Act prohibits large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, subject to certain exceptions. The proposed rule would clarify certain terms relevant to those restrictions, including “large institutional investor”; clarify the application of certain exceptions from the statutory prohibition; and clarify the statutory enforcement mechanism. The proposed rule is intended to provide clarity to market participants and other stakeholders on the application of the statute before the effective date of the ROAD Act.
items.title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Prohibition on Large Institutional Investor Purchases of Single-Family Homes

items.summary: In response to a request from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators), NHTSA is announcing a 30-day extension of the public comment period for the Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) published on September 22, 2026. The SNPRM supplements NHTSA's September 2023 notice of proposed rulemaking to amend NHTSA's regulations to include an advanced crash test dummy (the Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint (THOR) 50th percentile adult male) by requesting comment on specifying an additional spine configuration and an alternative to the face foam, and announcing the availability of additional documents. The comment period for the SNPRM was originally scheduled to end on October 22, 2026. It will now end on November 21, 2026.
items.title: Part 572; Anthropomorphic Test Devices; Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint 50th Percentile Adult Male Dummy (THOR-50M); Extension of Comment Period

items.summary: H.R. 1382 amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to restructure the San Francisco Bay restoration program, expanding eligible recipients and changing from grants to contracts and other funding mechanisms. Federal contributions are limited to 75 percent of project costs, with non-Federal entities required to provide at least 25 percent of funding from non-Federal sources. The bill prohibits federal funds from entities domiciled in or partnered with countries designated as foreign countries of concern.
items.title: 119 HR 1382 RH: To amend the Federal Water Pollution Control Act with respect to San Francisco Bay restoration, and for other purposes.
